title: FactorySchedule
description: A cron schedule that starts a Software Factory workflow: a cron trigger node in the workflow's graph whose id is metadata.name (at most 40 characters). Applying one saves and publishes a new version of the workflow, the same as adding the schedule on the Schedules tab, and creates or updates the timer that fires it; the workflow must be published and must not hold an unpublished draft. A cron trigger node the workflow already has under that id is adopted. Removing the document removes the node and its timer and publishes the workflow again.

workflow.description: The metadata.name of a FactoryWorkflow: the workflow the schedule starts.

cron.description: When the workflow runs: five cron fields (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week) of numbers, ranges, lists and steps. Day of month and day of week cannot both be restricted.

timezone.description: The IANA time zone the cron fields are read in, such as Australia/Melbourne. Defaults to UTC.

runsOn.description: The timer that fires the schedule: aws (an EventBridge Scheduler schedule) or cloudflare (a Worker cron trigger, for workflows that run in a Pix Sandbox). Defaults to aws.

overlap.description: What happens when the previous run is still going at the next fire. Defaults to skip_if_running.

enabled.description: Whether the schedule fires. A schedule of a workflow that is switched off fires but starts nothing.

title.description: The trigger node's title in the builder. Left out, the node is titled with metadata.name.

startAt.description: The ids of the steps in the workflow's graph the schedule leads to: one edge from the trigger to each, in this order.

priority.description: The run's priority, 1 (highest) to 5, when runs wait for capacity.
